# Welcome {.unnumbered}

Postgres is usually introduced as the place where an application keeps its rows. This book is
about everything else it turns out to be: a vector store, a job queue, a message broker, the
source of a change stream, the thing a permission spec is applied to. Each chapter takes one of
those roles, asks what it really costs, and answers with a measurement rather than a slogan.

All of it comes from one repository, [postgres-lab](https://github.com/deburky/postgres-lab): a set
of Docker containers (Postgres 16 and 18 with pgvector and friends, a replica, PgBouncer, Apache
Doris), a small FastAPI app that searches the SQLAlchemy documentation, and a notebook per topic.
Every number in the text was produced by one of those notebooks on a laptop, and the notebooks
themselves are in the appendix with their outputs, so you can check any claim against the run
that made it.

## The map

::: {.map}
::: {}
**Postgres from Python**

SQLAlchemy sync and async, JSONB documents, PgBouncer, and Postgres in WebAssembly for tests.
:::
::: {}
**Search**

pgvector from four distances to three index types (HNSW, DiskANN, PRISM), and loading vectors fast.
:::
::: {}
**Queues**

Two designs for a queue in a table: pgqueuer's heartbeats and pgmq's visibility timeouts.
:::
::: {}
**Moving data**

Logical replication from one Postgres to another, and into Apache Doris with its built-in CDC.
:::
::: {}
**Access and operations**

Roles and grants as code with Pulumi and pgsesame, and the same servers on local Kubernetes.
:::
:::

## How to read it

Every chapter has the same shape: the idea in a few paragraphs, the experiment that tests it,
what the experiment found, and the traps. The chapters stand alone; read them in any order. When
a chapter says "the notebook", it means the one linked at its end, rendered in the appendix.

Two pages are interactive. The queue scene above and the vector search city in
[Chapter 1](chapters/sqlalchemy.qmd) replay traces recorded from the lab's app: real workers,
real `NOTIFY`s, real HNSW walks, played back in your browser with no server behind them.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Run it yourself

Clone the repository, `cp .env.example .env`, `uv sync`, `just db`. That gives you Postgres 16 with
pgvector on `localhost:5432`, and every chapter's notebook runs from there (a few need a second
server, named in the chapter). [Running the lab](chapters/running-the-lab.qmd) has the details.
:::
